facts.label: How billing is counted
facts.value: Main outbound SES plan charge is per recipient email sent, not per stored subscriber. To, CC, and BCC addresses count individually toward sending quotas; SES plan pricing says outbound mail is charged per recipient.

facts.label: How billing is counted
facts.value: New-account plan charges use monthly email volume tiers applied marginally. The current USD page says inbound Mail Manager emails and outbound sends use independent tier volume counts.

facts.label: Free plan and trial limits
facts.value: For new AWS accounts created on or after 2025-07-15, AWS replaced the legacy 12-month Free Tier with up to USD $200 in account credits and a Free plan lasting up to six months or credit exhaustion. Eligible credits can apply to SES; they are not free SES sending. Accounts created before the cutoff retain legacy account-level terms.

facts.label: Free plan and trial limits
facts.value: The SES-specific 3,000 email-message-charge monthly free tier for the first 12 months ended for new customers on 2026-07-21. Existing enrolled accounts keep the remaining benefit in their 12-month period.

facts.label: Free plan and trial limits
facts.value: AWS European Sovereign Cloud pricing still includes a 3,000-message deduction in its sample calculation. Whether this is still available to new SES customers in that cloud is unclear because the newer central AWS announcement says the SES free tier ended for new customers and does not state a cloud exception.

facts.label: Paid entry price and commitment
facts.value: Essentials (default for new accounts and qualifying inactive account-region combinations): USD $0.16 per 1,000 emails in the first 10 million/month; $0.14 per 1,000 in the next 90 million; $0.11 per 1,000 above 100 million. Marginal tiers. Main USD table does not name a service Region.

facts.label: Paid entry price and commitment
facts.value: Pro: USD $0.22 per 1,000 in the first 10 million/month, $0.17 per 1,000 in the next 90 million, and $0.12 per 1,000 above 100 million, plus USD $105 per account per Region per month. The variable USD rates do not name a Region.

facts.label: Paid entry price and commitment
facts.value: Enterprise: USD $0.23 per 1,000 in the first 10 million/month, $0.18 per 1,000 in the next 90 million, and $0.13 per 1,000 above 100 million, plus USD $500 per account per Region per month. The variable USD rates do not name a Region.

facts.label: Paid entry price and commitment
facts.value: À-la-carte outbound: USD $0.10 per 1,000 emails plus USD $0.12 per GB of attachment data. Accounts can switch to à-la-carte; AWS says the current USD table is pay-as-you-go with no minimum usage or upfront commitment. The rate table does not identify a specific Region.

facts.label: Paid entry price and commitment
facts.value: AWS European Sovereign Cloud publishes a separate EUR à-la-carte table: €0.09868 per 1,000 outbound emails and €0.118 per GB of attachment data. The SES page does not identify a specific endpoint Region; its account portal is for AWS European Sovereign Cloud.

facts.label: Paid entry price and commitment
facts.value: AWS's European Sovereign Cloud SES page says there are no subscriptions and only lists à-la-carte pricing; the central 2026 pricing announcement says the new plans apply to SES regions except UAE and Bahrain. The pages do not explain this difference.

facts.label: Paid entry price and commitment
facts.value: Pricing-plan availability exclusions: AWS says its plans are available where SES is available except the Middle East (UAE) and Middle East (Bahrain) Regions. Some individual features have additional region exclusions.

facts.label: Paid entry price and commitment
facts.value: Current public USD SES page does not show a region selector or regional rows for the per-email rates. AWS's Price List documentation says price lists can be region-filtered, but a regional SES price could not be established from the public SES price page.

facts.label: Overage, caps, and rollover
facts.value: SES charges for metered sends under the selected plan; there is no monthly contact allowance or rollover in the pay-as-you-go pricing model. Price tiers apply marginally.

facts.label: Overage, caps, and rollover
facts.value: Daily sending quota is a hard limit; SES rejects an over-quota send request. Exceeding the per-second rate can lead to throttling. These are region-specific account quotas, not monthly included email allowances.

facts.label: Overage, caps, and rollover
facts.value: A dedicated SES spending cap or automatic monthly spend-stop control was not found in SES pricing, billing, or quota documentation checked.

facts.label: Total-cost extras
facts.value: Outbound message data is an additional SES charge. AWS's own Essentials example uses 32KB per email and charges USD $0.12/GB; attachment data may add cost at the same listed rate. The USD page does not name a specific SES Region for this rate.

facts.label: Total-cost extras
facts.value: Pro and Enterprise add USD $105/account/Region/month and USD $500/account/Region/month respectively. These fixed plan fees are separate from usage charges.

facts.label: Total-cost extras
facts.value: Standard dedicated IPs cost USD $24.95 per IP per month. Managed dedicated IPs cost USD $15 per account per month plus a per-email fee; the first 10 million tier is USD $0.08/1,000. Pro and Enterprise include managed-IP capability; Essentials has it as an add-on. The USD table does not name an SES Region for these rates.

facts.label: Total-cost extras
facts.value: SES deliverability and validation features differ by plan. The central plan table includes SES deliverability in all three plans; Pro and Enterprise add managed IPs and validations, and Essentials can add them. À-la-carte feature rates are separate.

facts.label: Total-cost extras
facts.value: AWS lists Global Deliverability at USD $1,250 per account per Region/month under à-la-carte pricing; Essentials lists it as an add-on while Pro and Enterprise include a defined monthly package.

facts.label: Total-cost extras
facts.value: Other AWS charges can apply for compute and data transfer from EC2, incoming-mail storage in S3, notifications through SNS, and custom CloudWatch dashboards or metrics. These are separate AWS products and excluded from SES-only examples.

facts.label: Total-cost extras
facts.value: Taxes and payment-currency conversion depend on AWS account billing location and agreement; the published USD figures are before any account-specific tax or conversion.

facts.label: Fees, processors, and payout access
facts.value: Not applicable: SES has no reader payment processor, platform revenue share, creator payout, or paid-newsletter billing feature.

facts.label: Technical sending limits
facts.value: Sandbox limit in each AWS Region: up to 200 recipients per rolling 24-hour period and 1 email per second; only verified recipients or the mailbox simulator can be used.

facts.label: Technical sending limits
facts.value: After production access, daily and per-second quotas vary by use case and Region. Users can request increases in Support Center; another Region may have different limits and sandbox status.

facts.label: Technical sending limits
facts.value: A message can have up to 50 recipients. SES v1 API max size is 10 MB after base64 encoding; SES v2 API and SMTP max is 40 MB after encoding. Messages above 10 MB may be bandwidth-throttled.

facts.label: Technical sending limits
facts.value: Exceeding a daily quota causes SES to reject a send; exceeding the per-second rate may be throttled. AWS recommends a separate SendEmail call per recipient.

facts.label: Countries, markets, and languages
facts.value: SES recipient destinations and AWS account eligibility are different questions. AWS lists SES regions, but the pages checked do not give a complete country-by-country customer signup or billing eligibility list.

facts.label: Countries, markets, and languages
facts.value: The SES production-access form offers English or Japanese for review communications. This does not establish every AWS console or support language.

facts.label: Countries, markets, and languages
facts.value: AWS European Sovereign Cloud support lists English, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, and Spanish. This is support coverage for that cloud, not all AWS regions.

facts.label: Entry and approval rules
facts.value: Requires an AWS account. New SES accounts start in the sandbox separately in each region. In the sandbox, users must verify sender identities and may send only to verified recipients or the SES mailbox simulator.

facts.label: Entry and approval rules
facts.value: To request production access, provide the sending type, website URL, contact email, and preferred review language; confirm that recipients explicitly requested mail and that bounce and complaint notifications will be handled. AWS says it provides an initial response within 96 hours; a decision can take longer if it needs more information.

facts.label: Entry and approval rules
facts.value: Production access removes recipient-verification restrictions, but not the requirement to verify each From, Source, Sender, or Return-Path identity.

facts.label: Entry and approval rules
facts.value: AWS prohibits sending unsolicited mass email and may investigate or disable access for a policy violation.

facts.label: Entry and approval rules
facts.value: AWS may suspend SES access for abusive or low-quality mail, bounces, complaints, or invalid feedback addresses; delivery failure outside AWS control does not cancel payment obligations.

facts.label: Email jobs
facts.value: Sends transactional and marketing email through SES API, SMTP, or an AWS SDK.

facts.label: Email jobs
facts.value: SES offers contact lists, topics, templates, and bulk-send APIs, but does not provide a full visual newsletter campaign workflow. Users build their own campaign authoring, audience workflow, and scheduling.

facts.label: Email jobs
facts.value: Mail Manager handles inbound email processing and routing as a distinct SES feature with separate metered charges.

facts.label: Hosting and sender dependency
facts.value: Hosted AWS service; no mail server or separate email sender is required. Connect an application to the SES API or SMTP endpoint.

facts.label: Hosting and sender dependency
facts.value: Customer is responsible for application, content, list acquisition, campaign design, scheduling, and event processing. Other AWS services are optional and separately billed.

facts.label: Paid newsletters
facts.value: Not applicable: SES can deliver messages for a paid newsletter built by the customer, but it does not charge readers, manage paid access, or provide paid-newsletter subscription tiers.

facts.label: Consent and unsubscribe controls
facts.value: SES requires explicitly requested recipients for production marketing sending. AWS's review form asks the user to confirm opt-in and bounce/complaint processes; unsolicited mass email is prohibited.

facts.label: Consent and unsubscribe controls
facts.value: Native topic preferences and unsubscribe management are available if the sender specifies the contact list/topic. SES can add List-Unsubscribe and one-click headers plus a footer link; one recipient per message is required for SES to add these links. Unsubscribed contacts are blocked for that topic/list.

facts.label: Consent and unsubscribe controls
facts.value: A hosted signup form or double-opt-in workflow was not established in the SES contact-list and subscription docs checked. Customers can use APIs/imports and must provide their own signup flow.

facts.label: Consent and unsubscribe controls
facts.value: Account-level suppression covers hard bounces and complaints, separately from marketing unsubscribes. It is region-specific and can be queried through SES API workflows.

facts.label: Custom domains and branding
facts.value: Sender identities can be email addresses or domains. A domain identity must be verified in each AWS Region where it will send. Easy DKIM, BYODKIM, and a custom MAIL FROM domain are supported.

facts.label: Custom domains and branding
facts.value: AWS Route 53 is optional for DNS changes and is separately priced; a third-party DNS host can publish SES verification records.

facts.label: Custom domains and branding
facts.value: SES does not add a newsletter website domain or publication identity. Message branding is customer-created in content/templates; the AWS domain may be used for SES-managed unsubscribe/tracking functions.

facts.label: Writing and template tools
facts.value: SES supports raw text and HTML messages and reusable email templates with subject, text, HTML, and personalization data through API/CLI.

facts.label: Writing and template tools
facts.value: No drag-and-drop newsletter editor or Markdown campaign editor was found in SES product pages, template docs, or API guides checked.

facts.label: Audience targeting
facts.value: SES contact lists support one list per AWS account, up to 20 topics, contact attributes, and querying by topic and subscription status.

facts.label: Audience targeting
facts.value: A native behavioral or rule-based dynamic segmentation builder was not established in list-management or API docs checked. Users can filter contacts in their application and send through SES.

facts.label: Automation and event triggers
facts.value: SES sends when called by an application. A native journey builder with delays, branching, or payment-triggered sequences is not documented; customers can connect SES APIs to separate AWS or external workflow services.

facts.label: Automation and event triggers
facts.value: Native campaign scheduling and automation run limits are not published for SES as a delivery API.

facts.label: API, SMTP, and integrations
facts.value: Send through SES v1/v2 API, SMTP, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. AWS lists SDKs for C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Kotlin, .NET, PHP, PowerShell, Python, Ruby, Rust, SAP ABAP, and Swift.

facts.label: API, SMTP, and integrations
facts.value: SES SMTP endpoints, API endpoints, and credentials are region-specific. SMTP credentials are different from general AWS credentials.

facts.label: API, SMTP, and integrations
facts.value: AWS documents integrations with S3, SNS, CloudWatch, Firehose, Lambda, EventBridge, and CloudTrail for receiving, notifications, event delivery, or auditing; each is a separate service.

facts.label: Events, retries, and debugging
facts.value: Event publishing supports send, delivery, bounce, complaint, reject, delay, subscription, open, click, and rendering-failure events through configuration sets and selected destinations. AWS requires feedback notifications or event publishing to track bounces and complaints.

facts.label: Events, retries, and debugging
facts.value: A successful SendEmail response means SES accepted the request, not that it reached the inbox. It returns a message ID; callers should keep their own mapping. Rarely, SES may accept mail even when the caller sees an error, so an application retry can create a duplicate send.

facts.label: Events, retries, and debugging
facts.value: SES retries soft bounces for an extended period; it does not retry hard bounces except DNS lookup failures. A universal retry-duration value was not stated in pages checked.

facts.label: Events, retries, and debugging
facts.value: SES receiving can route inbound email to S3 or send content in an SNS notification for customer processing; SES does not provide IMAP mailbox access.

facts.label: Domain authentication
facts.value: Sender domain or email identity verification is required. Easy DKIM is managed by SES and uses DNS records; BYODKIM is also supported. Identity and DKIM setup are repeated for each sending Region.

facts.label: Domain authentication
facts.value: SPF and DMARC records are configured in DNS by the domain owner. A custom MAIL FROM domain requires matching MX and SPF setup; DMARC is not automatically created by SES.

facts.label: Bounces, complaints, and suppression
facts.value: Account-level suppression can retain hard-bounce and complaint recipients; it is per account and AWS Region. Newer accounts default to both reasons, while older accounts may have to enable it. Suppressed sends still count against daily quota.

facts.label: Bounces, complaints, and suppression
facts.value: AWS recommends keeping bounce rate below 2%; at 5% or greater it places an account under review and at 10% or greater it may pause sending. Complaint rate should stay below 0.1%; at 0.1% AWS places an account under review and at 0.5% it may pause sending. Rates use representative sending volume, not a fixed period.

facts.label: Bounces, complaints, and suppression
facts.value: AWS may suspend or terminate SES access for policy or reputation problems, and service terms state that delivery failure outside AWS's control does not cancel payment obligations.

facts.label: Email streams and IP choices
facts.value: SES does not sell separate transactional and marketing products; both use outbound SES. Customers can separate configuration sets, tenants, and dedicated IP pools to manage sending and reputation.

facts.label: Email streams and IP choices
facts.value: Standard dedicated IPs are customer-managed. Managed IPs are warmed and scaled by SES; Pro and Enterprise include managed-IP capability and Essentials lists it as an add-on. Shared IP is the default if no dedicated IP is selected.

facts.label: Reporting and tracking choices
facts.value: SES provides counts for sends, deliveries, bounces, complaints, rejects, delays, subscriptions, opens, and clicks through console metrics, event publishing, CloudWatch, or Virtual Deliverability Manager.

facts.label: Reporting and tracking choices
facts.value: Open/click tracking can be enabled through Virtual Deliverability Manager/configuration sets. SES uses a tracking pixel and wrapped links; users can omit the pixel by sending without a tracked configuration set.

facts.label: Reporting and tracking choices
facts.value: SES collects open and click metrics for 60 days after each email is sent. No complete bot or privacy-proxy filtering method was established in the tracking and metrics docs checked.

facts.label: Own-server setup and work
facts.value: Not applicable: SES is hosted by AWS. Customers build applications and integrations but do not install or operate the SES mail server.

facts.label: Growth and newsletter income tools
facts.value: Not applicable: SES does not include referrals, audience recommendations, ads, sponsorship marketplace, or creator monetization.

facts.label: List ownership and export
facts.value: SES offers one contact list per AWS account, up to 20 topics, contact attributes, and API access to subscribed, unsubscribed, and topic-specific contacts. Contacts can be imported through an S3 CSV/JSON import job or console.

facts.label: List ownership and export
facts.value: Contact records can be retrieved through the ListContacts API; the account-level suppression list can be read through API and console, and templates can be listed and retrieved through SES v2.

facts.label: List ownership and export
facts.value: AWS's current service terms say SES may store and scan SES email/content for abuse and security prevention. AWS customer agreements govern customer content; the export procedure does not transfer data outside AWS by itself.

facts.label: List ownership and export
facts.value: A single complete export including all contacts, consent history, message bodies, tracking events, suppression entries, and customer-side event destinations was not documented as one operation.

facts.label: Paid-subscriber migration
facts.value: Not applicable: SES does not manage reader payments or subscription entitlements that could be migrated. Contact and suppression records can be retrieved separately through APIs.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: SES resources and identities are regional. Resources used for receiving email must generally be in the same Region as the SES endpoint, except S3 buckets. Customer selects the Region for stored resources.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: AWS DPA is incorporated into AWS Service Terms for customer data processing. AWS describes transfers outside the selected Region as limited to providing/maintaining service, following customer instruction, or complying with law.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: SES terms allow AWS or third-party providers to store and scan SES email/content to detect spam, phishing, malware, and unwanted items. SES receiving content may be routed to user-selected S3 or SNS destinations.

facts.label: Data location and privacy terms
facts.value: A complete per-message map of backup, abuse-review, and temporary processing locations is not published in SES pages checked.

facts.label: Retention and deletion
facts.value: SES open/click metrics remain available for 60 days. Suppression addresses remain until removed, subject to the documented 90-day clearing condition after sending is paused.

facts.label: Retention and deletion
facts.value: Customers can delete contacts, suppression addresses, templates, identities, and configured destinations through console or API; data already exported to S3 or Firehose must be deleted there separately.

facts.label: Retention and deletion
facts.value: A single retention period for all SES contact records, email content, abuse scans, events, and backups was not published.

facts.label: Account safeguards
facts.value: IAM controls access to SES API and console operations. SES can use scoped permissions and separate credentials; SMTP credentials differ from general AWS credentials and are Region-specific.

facts.label: Account safeguards
facts.value: AWS supports multi-factor authentication for AWS account and IAM access.

facts.label: Name, official site, and status
facts.value: Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES), marketed as Amazon SES; active hosted service.

facts.label: Name, official site, and status
facts.value: SES is a regional AWS service. Account setup, identities, quotas, SMTP credentials, and suppression lists are region-specific.

facts.label: Support and reliability evidence
facts.value: Basic AWS Support is included and provides documentation, AWS re:Post/community, AWS Health, and account/billing help. Technical support channels vary by paid AWS Support plan.

facts.label: Support and reliability evidence
facts.value: SES has a published 99.9% monthly availability commitment for each AWS Region in the AWS User Engagement SLA, subject to SLA exclusions and service-credit terms. The SLA was last updated 2024-07-24 and lists SES separately from Pinpoint.

facts.label: Support and reliability evidence
facts.value: Public AWS Health provides service status; an SES production-access request gets an initial response within 96 hours, with longer resolution possible if AWS requests information.

facts.label: Source license and maintenance
facts.value: Not applicable: Amazon SES is a managed AWS service, not customer-installable source software.

facts.label: Acquisition, shutdown, or sunset evidence
facts.value: AWS's central services-in-sunset list names Amazon Pinpoint with end of support 2026-10-30; it does not list Amazon SES as shutting down.

facts.label: Acquisition, shutdown, or sunset evidence
facts.value: The official AWS News Blog lists 2026 posts tagged Amazon SES, including current SES operations and product updates; no SES shutdown notice appears in the product-tagged results checked.

facts.label: Acquisition, shutdown, or sunset evidence
facts.value: No SES shutdown, sunset, or acquisition notice was found in the AWS Messaging Blog and AWS What's New searches or the sunset and service-term pages checked.

facts.label: Owner and home region
facts.value: Amazon Web Services, Inc. and affiliates operate AWS services; parent is Amazon.com, Inc. Contracting party varies by account location.

facts.label: Owner and home region
facts.value: For EU customers using AWS European Sovereign Cloud, AWS identifies Amazon Web Services EMEA SARL in Luxembourg as contracting party; the sovereign cloud is a separate AWS environment.

subs.math: 4,000 emails a month, counted per recipient, cost $1.60 in usage charges. The minimum deposit is $15, and unused balance carries forward.
20,000 emails a month, counted per recipient, cost $8 in usage charges. The minimum deposit is $15, and unused balance carries forward.
40,000 emails a month at $0.40 per 1,000 = $16 in usage charges, which is more than the $15 minimum deposit.
200,000 emails a month at $0.40 per 1,000 = $80 in usage charges.

appmail.math: 3,000 emails a month, counted per recipient, cost $1.20 in usage charges, about 100 a day over 30 days. The minimum deposit is $15, and unused balance carries forward.
10,000 emails a month, counted per recipient, cost $4 in usage charges, about 333 a day over 30 days. The minimum deposit is $15, and unused balance carries forward.
50,000 emails a month at $0.40 per 1,000 = $20 in usage charges, about 1,667 a day over 30 days, before tax.
100,000 emails a month at $0.40 per 1,000 = $40 in usage charges, about 3,334 a day over 30 days, before tax.

facts.label: Billing unit
facts.value: Email marketing plans specify a monthly email volume per workspace; each workspace has separate billing. Contact capacity is a different limit.

facts.label: Contacts by plan
facts.value: Free: 5,000 contacts; Starter: unlimited contacts subject to Fair Use; Custom: custom contact allowance.

facts.label: Email counting in automations
facts.value: Each email sent by an automation's Send Email action uses the same monthly email quota as campaign sends.

facts.label: System email billing
facts.value: System automations such as confirmation and preference-management emails do not count toward billing limits, according to the help page.

facts.label: Duplicate and billable-contact rules
facts.value: Contact deduplication is listed on all plans, but exact duplicate matching and how unsubscribed, bounced, or duplicate records affect any Fair Use assessment are not explained in the pricing/help pages checked.

facts.label: Ongoing Free plan
facts.value: Free: USD $0/month; 1,000 email sends per month; 5,000 contacts; 2 domains; 1 user; 1 workspace; 3 segments; 1 automation; 5,000 events/month; 25,000 AI credits.

facts.label: Free campaign features
facts.value: Free plan lists campaign broadcasts, scheduling, A/B testing, editor, link tracking, unsubscribes, preferences, forms, API, and analytics.

facts.label: Free plan gates
facts.value: Free allows 1 automation and 3 segments; conversion tracking is not included in the matrix. RSS automation campaigns are marked Coming Soon across all plans.

facts.label: Starter plan limits
facts.value: Starter: USD $15/month at the displayed 5,000-email monthly selection; 5,000 email sends/month; unlimited contacts subject to Fair Use; 3 domains; 3 users; 25 segments; 15 automations; 25,000 events/month; 250,000 AI credits.

facts.label: Custom plan limits
facts.value: Custom is quote-priced and lists 3,000,000+ emails/month, custom contacts, unlimited domains, users, segments, automations, and events, custom AI credits, and 24/7 priority support.

facts.label: Free trial and card requirement
facts.value: The public registration page says no credit card is required and the pricing page lists a continuing Free plan. A separate time-limited trial was not described.

facts.label: SMS allowance
facts.value: SMS is listed as pay as you go on Free, Starter, and Custom, with coverage stated as 130+ countries; SMS charges are separate from the email quota.

facts.label: Paid entry price
facts.value: Starter at the displayed 5,000 emails/month: $15 USD per month. Free is $0 USD per month.

facts.label: Tax treatment
facts.value: Published plan prices exclude applicable taxes, levies, and duties.

facts.label: Billing interval and payment
facts.value: Card subscriptions are charged monthly. Terms also allow monthly or annual billing, but the public pricing extraction did not expose an annual amount or savings.

facts.label: Alternative payment commitment
facts.value: Cryptocurrency and bank-transfer arrangements require contacting support and have a six-month minimum, paid upfront for the full period.

facts.label: Cancellation and refund
facts.value: Terms say a customer can cancel at any time, with cancellation effective immediately and no later billing cycles charged. A new customer may request a refund within 14 days subject to the Refund Policy's use restrictions.

facts.label: Above-quota behavior
facts.value: Terms say excess usage may incur charges specified by the plan; no exact overage rate, automatic upgrade rule, or pause behavior was published in pricing, terms, billing help, or automation help.

facts.label: Usage reset and rollover
facts.value: A monthly allowance is specified, but whether unused email sends roll over or when the quota resets was not stated in the pricing, Terms, or billing help checked.

facts.label: Spending cap
facts.value: No customer-configurable overage spending cap was found in pricing, Terms, billing help, or quota help.

facts.label: Sending and hosting extras
facts.value: No separate SMTP provider or web-hosting plan is required for CampaignLark email campaigns. A customer still needs a usable sender domain and may incur separate domain-registration costs.

facts.label: Domains and user costs
facts.value: Free includes 2 domains and 1 user; Starter includes 3 domains and 3 users; Custom lists custom domain/user limits.

facts.label: SMS extra
facts.value: SMS campaigns are pay-as-you-go on all three plans; the email plan price does not include a stated SMS message bundle.

facts.label: Taxes and payment fees
facts.value: Published prices exclude tax. Subscription payments use card by default; cryptocurrency and bank transfer are manual alternatives. Processor charges passed to the subscriber beyond the listed plan amount were not established.

facts.label: Separate Maileroo subscription
facts.value: CampaignLark is separately billed by workspace. Maileroo's Jan 2026 announcement says existing Maileroo lifetime plans and pricing commitments remain unchanged; no Maileroo plan is stated as a prerequisite for CampaignLark.

facts.label: Paid newsletter fees and payouts
facts.value: Reader-payment processors, platform fees, payout timing, and supported creator payout countries were not described in the product pricing, Terms, or help pages checked.

facts.label: Subscription billing processor
facts.value: The DPA names Stripe for subscription billing, payment processing, tax compliance, and customer invoicing; the billing help also says cryptocurrency and bank transfer are available on request.

facts.label: Email send caps
facts.value: Free allows 1,000 email sends/month; Starter 5,000/month at the displayed selection; Custom starts at 3,000,000+ emails/month with custom pricing/allowance.

facts.label: API and event limits
facts.value: API request rate is 100/second/workspace; Event API maximum ingestion is 100 events/second/workspace plus the plan's monthly event allowance.

facts.label: Send speed, payload, and test-email caps
facts.value: Per-second campaign delivery rate, message size, attachment limit, and numeric hourly/daily test-email limits were not published in the campaign API docs checked.

facts.label: Customer country eligibility
facts.value: Minimum age is 18. No complete list of allowed or blocked customer countries was published in the terms, pricing, billing help, or signup page checked.

facts.label: Email delivery destinations
facts.value: Email-recipient country restrictions were not published in the pricing, terms, AUP, or developer introduction pages checked. The pricing page's 130+ countries statement applies to SMS coverage, not email delivery.

facts.label: Interface and support languages
facts.value: English public site and help center were checked. A complete list of supported interface or support languages is not published.

facts.label: Signup route and free access
facts.value: Self-service account registration is offered without a credit card; an ongoing Free plan is listed.

facts.label: Sending approval
facts.value: Each new workspace must request and receive sending approval before email campaigns can be sent. Approval is requested from the workspace dashboard.

facts.label: Approval review and timing
facts.value: Review asks for business details, intended email use, and contact-source type. Incomplete answers can delay or lead to rejection; no guaranteed review time is published.

facts.label: Minimum customer age
facts.value: Service terms say users must be at least 18 and legally able to contract.

facts.label: Email jobs
facts.value: Newsletter broadcasts, promotional campaigns, audience segmentation, and marketing automation

facts.label: Other channels and email API scope
facts.value: SMS campaigns and APIs for contacts, campaign operations, events, and conversions are also offered. No general-purpose transactional email API is documented as a separate CampaignLark product.

facts.label: Hosting and sending
facts.value: Hosted SaaS; CampaignLark includes sending against each workspace's monthly email allowance. No customer-operated server or separate SMTP provider is required for documented campaigns.

facts.label: Maileroo company relationship
facts.value: Same legal operator: Maileroo Group Pty Ltd. CampaignLark is a separate product and brand, not a separate acquired company.

facts.label: Shared sending infrastructure
facts.value: CampaignLark says it removed the marketing product from the Maileroo ecosystem and isolated its infrastructure. Whether delivery uses any same providers, IP pools, or technical sending paths as Maileroo SMTP/API is not stated.

facts.label: Paid newsletters
facts.value: The official API feature page says newsletter tools can help creators “monetize,” but pricing and help pages checked do not explain native reader payments, paid tiers, access control, or subscription billing.

facts.label: Consent and list policy
facts.value: AUP permits permission-based email only, requiring valid, informed, verifiable consent or another lawful basis. Purchased, rented, scraped, appended, and third-party lists and cold outreach are prohibited.

facts.label: Unsubscribe and preference controls
facts.value: Unsubscribe management and preference management are listed on Free, Starter, and Custom. AUP requires a functional unsubscribe in each message.

facts.label: Signup forms and opt-in modes
facts.value: Inline and popup signup forms can show consent text, and support single or double opt-in. Form options can block proxy/VPN and disposable-email submissions.

facts.label: Contact status and suppressions
facts.value: API contact status distinguishes SUBSCRIBED, UNSUBSCRIBED, UNCONFIRMED, CLEANED, and COMPLAINED. AUP prohibits evading unsubscribe, suppression, bounce, or complaint protections.

facts.label: Consent enforcement thresholds
facts.value: AUP requires bounce rate below 5% and complaint rate below 0.1%; higher rates can cause restrictions, review, or suspension.

facts.label: Sending and tracking domains
facts.value: Custom sending and tracking domains are supported with DNS verification for SPF, DKIM, MX, and DMARC; docs say SSL is provisioned for tracking domains.

facts.label: Domain allowances
facts.value: Pricing lists 2 domains on Free, 3 on Starter, and Custom on Custom. Free CampaignLark domains and custom tracking domains with SSL are listed across plans.

facts.label: Brand removal
facts.value: Whether CampaignLark branding can be removed from email footers or hosted assets is not specified in the pricing and help pages checked.

facts.label: Mailbox requirement
facts.value: A sending domain can be configured in a workspace; whether an ordinary mailbox or separate mailbox subscription is required for replies was not specified.

facts.label: Email editor
facts.value: Pricing includes the Lark visual editor and custom HTML editor on all listed plans; help describes ready-made gallery templates and a responsive editing preview.

facts.label: Templates and reuse
facts.value: Reusable templates, saved blocks, and template gallery access are listed on all plans. Completed campaigns can be cloned into new drafts.

facts.label: HTML and test messages
facts.value: Users can compose with custom HTML and send a test email to one recipient before scheduling a campaign.

facts.label: Personalization
facts.value: Custom fields and merge tags support dynamic contact values; API templating docs advertise Handlebars variables, conditionals, and helpers.

facts.label: Tags and segments
facts.value: Contact tags can be manually assigned and used for campaigns and automation branches. Segments update dynamically from fields, tags, engagement, and activity with AND/OR conditions.

facts.label: Custom contact fields
facts.value: Default fields include email, first name, last name, phone, and country; custom fields support text, number, date, country, boolean, and single/multiple dropdown types.

facts.label: Plan gates for segments and contacts
facts.value: Free: 3 segments and 5,000 contacts; Starter: 25 segments and unlimited contacts subject to Fair Use; Custom: unlimited segments and custom contacts.

facts.label: Teams and workspaces
facts.value: Workspaces isolate contacts, campaigns, automations, templates, users, and billing; Free includes 1 workspace, Starter unlimited subject to Fair Use, and Custom custom.

facts.label: Automation availability and limits
facts.value: Visual multi-step journeys, behavioral triggers, conditional logic, events, waits, and analytics are listed across plans. Automation counts: Free 1, Starter 15, Custom unlimited.

facts.label: Trigger types
facts.value: Published triggers include subscriber actions, custom events, date-based triggers, field updates, tags, segments, and subscriptions.

facts.label: Custom event capacity
facts.value: Pricing lists 5,000 custom events/conversions on Free, 25,000 on Starter, and a custom/unlimited amount on Custom. Free and Starter top cards separately say 5,000 and 25,000 events/month.

facts.label: Email automation charging
facts.value: Email actions count as monthly email sending; system confirmation and preference automations themselves do not incur a separate charge.

facts.label: Exact workflow-run limit
facts.value: Pricing gives the number of automations that can be created, but no per-contact run, step, or execution cap was found in the pricing, API introduction, or automation help pages checked.

facts.label: Developer API
facts.value: REST API supports contacts, tags, fields, segments, events, campaign operations, domains, templates, conversions, and SMS campaigns.

facts.label: API authentication and access scope
facts.value: API uses a Bearer API key scoped to one workspace; help says users can restrict keys to allowed IP addresses, revoke, or roll a key.

facts.label: API, SMTP, and integrations
facts.value: Marketing API and webhooks are documented. CampaignLark SMTP relay support and specific prebuilt third-party integrations were not established; the launch announcement assigns SMTP and Email API focus to Maileroo.

facts.label: API request limits
facts.value: REST API: 100 requests per second per workspace; custom-event ingestion: maximum 100 events per second per workspace, subject to monthly plan event quota.

facts.label: SDKs and integrations directory
facts.value: API documentation is available, but an SDK list or named native app-integration catalog was not found in the docs introduction and integrations page checked.

facts.label: Outgoing webhooks
facts.value: Outgoing webhooks cover 15+ event types, include HMAC-SHA256 signatures, and retry up to 8 times with exponential backoff.

facts.label: Campaign and recipient history
facts.value: Campaign reports include delivered, opened, clicked, bounced, unsubscribed, and complained totals, link activity, and recipient-level email history.

facts.label: Inbound replies and message retries
facts.value: Incoming webhooks accept outside contact/event updates. Inbound reply routing, duplicate-send protection, and email delivery retry schedule were not documented in the API intro and webhook feature page checked.

facts.label: Domain authentication
facts.value: Docs state custom sending domains can be verified using SPF, DKIM, MX, and DMARC records.

facts.label: Authentication requirements and alignment
facts.value: The exact requirement for each record, SPF/DKIM alignment guarantees, and whether DMARC is mandatory for every account were not specified in the documentation intro or pricing page checked.

facts.label: Bounce and complaint tracking
facts.value: Pricing and reports include bounce and complaint tracking; AUP requires bounce below 5% and complaint rate below 0.1%.

facts.label: Suppression and unsubscribe status
facts.value: API contact status includes unsubscribed, cleaned, and complained states; AUP prohibits bypassing unsubscribe, suppression, bounce, and complaint protections.

facts.label: Bounce handling detail
facts.value: Retry rules for bounced messages, complaint-event handling time, and suppression-list export controls were not found in the reporting help, API introduction, or AUP checked.

facts.label: Sending streams and IP options
facts.value: CampaignLark describes isolated product infrastructure. Public pricing and sending documentation do not disclose shared vs dedicated IP choices, IP warm-up, or separate transactional/campaign streams.

facts.label: Maileroo sending relationship
facts.value: Maileroo states it remains focused on SMTP and Email API while its marketing tools moved to CampaignLark. The precise sender-provider and shared-IP relationship is not published.

facts.label: Campaign reporting
facts.value: Reports cover deliveries, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes, complaints, device, email provider, geography, and per-recipient history.

facts.label: Conversion tracking
facts.value: Conversion tracking is not listed for Free and is listed on Starter and Custom. API supports sending conversion events against campaign tracking identifiers.

facts.label: Tracking choices and bot filtering
facts.value: Ability to turn off open pixels or click rewrites and filtering of bot or privacy-proxy activity were not documented in the pricing, reporting help, or conversion docs checked.

facts.label: Tracking domains
facts.value: Custom tracking domains with SSL are listed on all plans.

facts.label: Own-server setup
facts.value: Not applicable: this product is vendor-hosted; customers configure a workspace, domains, contacts, and integrations rather than operating CampaignLark servers or backups.

facts.label: Creator monetization and growth
facts.value: Native paid-reader subscriptions, newsletter referrals, sponsorship marketplace, or ad placement were not documented. The marketing page's broad “monetize” wording was not enough to confirm any one of those tools.

facts.label: Vendor affiliate program
facts.value: CampaignLark has a separate affiliate program and agreement for referring new customers to CampaignLark.

facts.label: List export and transfer
facts.value: Pricing lists CSV import/export on all plans. Exact export fields, formats beyond CSV, consent-history completeness, and treatment of suppressions are not stated in the retrieved export material.

facts.label: Contact API access
facts.value: REST API supports searching, creating, updating, and deleting contacts, with field, tag, and email-status data. API keys are scoped to one workspace.

facts.label: Customer content ownership
facts.value: Terms say customers retain ownership of content submitted to the service, with a limited license to process, store, and transmit it to provide and improve the service.

facts.label: Paid-subscriber migration
facts.value: A supported migration of recurring reader subscriptions or payment relationships was not documented; the monetization claim itself is not backed by described subscriber billing.

facts.label: Data storage and processing region
facts.value: Terms say servers and customer data are in the EU. Privacy Policy says servers are in Germany and acknowledges processing by providers in other countries.

facts.label: Subprocessors and transfers
facts.value: DPA lists processors in the US, Germany, France, Ireland, Switzerland, Bulgaria, Netherlands, Hungary, and UK, and includes EU/UK/Swiss transfer provisions and Standard Contractual Clauses.

facts.label: Residency choice
facts.value: No customer-selectable region or separate email-storage, log, backup, and sending-region control was found in Terms, Privacy, DPA, or the docs intro.

facts.label: Privacy and processing agreement
facts.value: Privacy Policy and DPA are publicly linked. DPA describes CampaignLark as processor for contact, message, delivery, tracking, analytics, and campaign data, and provides change notice for subprocessors.

facts.label: Retention and deletion
facts.value: Terms say active-account data is retained as needed; after cancellation, email logs and analytics may remain up to 90 days, billing records as legally required, and deletion may be requested.

facts.label: Retention conflict by data type
facts.value: DPA specifies email content/attachments and metadata/logs up to 14 days, analytics up to 2 years or as configured, billing records at least 7 years, and backups up to 30 days. This differs from the Terms' up-to-90-day email logs/analytics statement.

facts.label: Login and team safeguards
facts.value: Two-factor authentication, passkeys, and roles/permissions are listed across all plans. DPA states MFA for administrative access and role-based access controls.

facts.label: API key safeguards
facts.value: API keys are workspace-scoped; users can restrict allowed IPs, revoke, or roll keys.

facts.label: Name, official site, and status
facts.value: CampaignLark; https://campaignlark.com/; active hosted email marketing product

facts.label: Product change and former name
facts.value: Maileroo's earlier email-marketing tools moved to CampaignLark; Maileroo was not rebranded. CampaignLark launch announcement is dated 2026-01-30; the company's changelog announced its arrival on 2026-02-08.

facts.label: Human support
facts.value: Email and live chat are listed on Free, Starter, and Custom. Dedicated account manager and 24/7 support are listed only for Custom.

facts.label: Service-level commitment
facts.value: SLA promises 99.90% monthly uptime for paid users; Free users are excluded. Eligible credits apply to future payments, and written claims are due within 10 business days.

facts.label: Public service status
facts.value: A CampaignLark status page was not located: attempted status.campaignlark.com and campaignlark.com/status; neither returned a page. The Maileroo status page was not treated as proof for the isolated CampaignLark service.

facts.label: Service availability terms
facts.value: Terms do not guarantee uninterrupted service; they allow planned or unplanned interruption. Paid SLA defines service credits and exclusions.

facts.label: Source license and maintenance
facts.value: Not applicable to the researched hosted CampaignLark SaaS: Terms grant limited access to the service and prohibit copying, reverse engineering, reselling, or sublicensing it; no self-hosted source license was offered in the product docs.

facts.label: History and launch
facts.value: CampaignLark launched as a standalone marketing product in February 2026 after Maileroo released a marketing product in 2024 and then separated and rebranded it.

facts.label: Public scale claim
facts.value: CampaignLark reports 100M+ monthly emails delivered and 85%+ inbox placement. These are vendor claims without a public measurement method on the pages checked.

facts.label: Owner and country
facts.value: Operator and owner named in legal terms: Maileroo Group Pty Ltd, an Australian company with registered office in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia.

facts.label: Relationship to Maileroo
facts.value: CampaignLark and Maileroo are products under Maileroo Group Pty Ltd; no separate company owner or acquisition was identified in the official pages checked.

facts.value: Standard starts at USD $20/month for up to 500 contacts on Mailchimp’s current Standard plan page; Transactional requires an active eligible monthly plan, so its base subscription is an additional cost

facts.label: Billing interval and currency
facts.value: Blocks recur monthly and are paid in advance; USD price table is before tax. A non-USD account is charged using Mailchimp’s unpublished exchange rate at payment processing.

facts.label: Dedicated IP price
facts.value: Optional dedicated IP is USD $29.95/month, plus the Transactional block and required Marketing-plan charges

facts.label: Promotion
facts.value: Pricing page advertises 50% off the Transactional monthly base price for 1M+ sends/40+ blocks for the first 12 months, with new-customer, plan, account-age, country and sales-contact conditions

facts.label: Included allowance, expiry and rollover
facts.value: Purchased blocks expire at the end of the billing month. Unused email credits do not roll over.

facts.label: Usage beyond allowance
facts.value: Account can stop sends at the limit or automatically buy additional blocks; top-off blocks are 25,000 sends and expire at cycle end. Automatic top-off is unlimited; a manual-purchase/alert setting is also available.

facts.label: Additional charges
facts.value: Dedicated IP is optional at $29.95/month. Applicable taxes may be added; other-currency billing uses an unpublished exchange rate. Customer also supplies a domain and DNS access.

facts.label: Marketing-plan cost separation
facts.value: Transactional blocks do not replace the required Standard/Premium monthly Marketing plan charge. Removing Transactional does not cancel Marketing billing; canceling/pause/downgrading Marketing can remove Transactional access.

facts.label: Fees, payment processors and payouts
facts.value: Not applicable: Transactional does not charge readers or pay out creator subscription revenue

facts.label: Monthly allowance and top-offs
facts.value: Monthly blocks are 25,000 sends each; extra blocks are optional auto-purchase or manual top-off. No rollover.

facts.label: Hourly quota and backlog
facts.value: Paid hourly quota is dynamic and depends on reputation and typical sending volume; excess messages queue. Backlog messages are deleted after 48 hours. Demo quota is 25 emails/hour.

facts.label: Batch and payload limits
facts.value: SMTP supports up to 1,000 recipients per send. API has no published recipient-count cap per call, but request JSON must be under 10 MB.

facts.label: API request-rate limit
facts.value: Numeric Transactional API requests-per-second/minute limit was not found in the Transactional API reference, developer docs, help pages, pricing or terms checked

facts.label: Attachments and maximum message size
facts.value: Attachment-specific and final encoded message-size limits were not stated in the outbound guide, API reference, help, pricing or terms pages checked

facts.label: Countries and markets
facts.value: Terms exclude comprehensively embargoed/sanctioned locations, including Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Russia and listed Ukrainian regions, plus restricted parties; a complete list of all eligible signup/payment countries was not located

facts.label: Interface and support languages
facts.value: Mailchimp lists English, Spanish, French, Portuguese, German and Italian for its website/help center and technical email/chat support; Transactional-specific interface language coverage is not separately specified

facts.label: Account and product access
facts.value: A Mailchimp account is required. Full Transactional email requires an active Standard or Premium monthly marketing plan (legacy Monthly plans are also named on current product/pricing pages) and purchase of email blocks. Marketing campaigns do not have to be run.

facts.label: One-time demo
facts.value: Eligible new Transactional users can use a one-time demo without buying blocks or upgrading to Standard/Premium; active Mailchimp account in good standing, verified sending domain, maximum 500 sends total, 25 per hour and 100 inbound messages per day

facts.label: Sending-domain setup
facts.value: Sending domain must be verified and configured with DKIM and a DMARC policy before authenticated sending; user must control its DNS

facts.label: Signup and approval
facts.value: Self-service purchase instructions are documented. No general manual account approval or review time is published; sending can be limited by reputation and content review

facts.label: Email jobs
facts.value: One-to-one, event-triggered application and commerce email, including password resets, receipts, order updates, account notices and appointment reminders

facts.label: Marketing campaigns
facts.value: Bulk marketing newsletters are not an allowed Transactional use; Mailchimp directs that use to Marketing campaigns

facts.label: Transactional SMS
facts.value: Transactional SMS is also offered, but is a separate channel requiring SMS Marketing access and SMS credits; not included in email block prices

facts.label: Hosting and sender dependency
facts.value: Hosted Mailchimp delivery service; customers connect with API or SMTP; customer application/database supplies recipient data

facts.label: Paid newsletters
facts.value: Not applicable: Transactional provides message delivery, not paid newsletter subscriptions, paywalls or creator billing

facts.label: Consent, opt-out and suppression
facts.value: Customer manages recipient records and consent. Transactional automatically rejects addresses after bounce, complaint or unsubscribe; an unsubscribe is scoped to the sender address. Bulk marketing through Transactional is prohibited.

facts.label: Sending domains and authentication
facts.value: Customer can use a verified sending domain/subdomain. DKIM and DMARC must be configured; a custom return-path domain can be set after configuration.

facts.label: SPF requirement
facts.value: The current Transactional authentication guide requires DKIM and DMARC but does not state that SPF is required for Transactional sending

facts.label: Branding and tracking domain
facts.value: Transactional templates can use customer branding; whether a custom link-tracking domain is available on all accounts is not established in the docs checked

facts.label: Template and writing tools
facts.value: Mailchimp template builder supports drag-and-drop templates and HTML coding; templates must be published to Transactional before API use

facts.label: Dynamic content
facts.value: API/SMTP templates support recipient-specific merge variables using Mailchimp merge tags or Handlebars; conditional helpers are documented

facts.label: Audience targeting
facts.value: Not applicable: no subscriber/audience store or newsletter segments are provided. Message tags and metadata support message reporting, not a managed audience.

facts.label: Event triggers and automation
facts.value: Customer application handles business/event logic and calls API/SMTP; Transactional supports scheduled messages and a rules engine reacting to send, delivery, bounce, open, click, unsubscribe, complaint, reject and inbound events

facts.label: API and SMTP
facts.value: Transactional email can be sent through its API or SMTP relay; API reference and official client-library directory are linked in the setup help

facts.label: Integrations
facts.value: Product supports direct API/SMTP connection and webhooks; other Mailchimp Marketing integrations are not evidence of a native Transactional connector

facts.label: Delivery events and webhook retries
facts.value: Webhooks include send, deferral, hard/soft bounce, delivery, open, click, spam, unsubscribe, reject, allow/deny-list sync and inbound events. Failed POST batches retry up to 20 times at 15–25 minute intervals; repeated failure disables the webhook.

facts.label: Inbound email
facts.value: Optional inbound processing receives, parses and forwards email data to the customer’s webhook; customer configures an exclusive subdomain/MX records

facts.label: Message logs and duplicate protection
facts.value: Recent successful and failed API calls are shown in logs; message resend is available. A general idempotency/deduplication window was not stated.

facts.label: Domain authentication
facts.value: DKIM signing and a DMARC policy are required for a sending domain. The minimum documented DMARC policy is v=DMARC1; p=none.

facts.label: Bounce, complaint and suppression behavior
facts.value: Bounces, spam complaints and unsubscribes automatically create rejection-denylist entries. Hard-bounce entries last 7 days; soft bounces 24 hours; complaints/unsubscribes 1 year; manual entries do not expire.

facts.label: Suppression list export
facts.value: Rejection denylist and allowlist can be exported from the app or via API; export download links expire after 7 days

facts.label: Transactional/marketing separation
facts.value: Transactional is an API/SMTP product for triggered messages; Marketing campaigns handle bulk mail. The terms prohibit bulk marketing through Transactional.

facts.label: IP choice and warm-up
facts.value: Shared IP is the default. Dedicated IP is optional at $29.95/month, typically manually approved in 24–48 hours; optional warm-up gradually increases use over the next month.

facts.label: Reporting and metrics
facts.value: Per-message reports cover delivery, bounces/rejections, opens and clicks; aggregate statistics are stored indefinitely. Tracking can be switched off globally or per message.

facts.label: Automated-open/click filtering
facts.value: Whether Transactional reports filter privacy-proxy, bot or automated opens/clicks was not specified in Activity and Reports, webhooks, FAQ, pricing or terms checked

facts.label: Own-server setup
facts.value: Not applicable as a self-host product. Customer must operate its application and manage DNS; Mailchimp runs the service.

facts.label: Newsletter growth and income tools
facts.value: Not applicable to this transactional delivery product; referrals, recommendation networks, ad placement and sponsorship sales are not part of the described Transactional feature set

facts.label: Contact-list ownership and export
facts.value: Customer retains its own contact system; Transactional does not store a subscriber list. Message content can be viewed/resend for 30 days; overall aggregate stats are retained indefinitely. Activity/report data can be exported via the app/API.

facts.label: Paid-subscriber migration
facts.value: Not applicable: no paid newsletter subscriptions or reader-payment relationships are managed by this product

facts.label: Data location and processing
facts.value: Mailchimp’s DPA permits processing in the US and other countries where Mailchimp, affiliates or subprocessors operate. Mailchimp’s Europe transfer help says its servers are in the US and data may be processed outside Europe. Transactional-specific data-type/region mapping is not published in these pages.

facts.label: Privacy terms and deletion
facts.value: Current Standard Terms incorporate the DPA and Global Privacy Statement. The DPA describes return/deletion after termination but excludes data held in backups until later deletion under policy.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Sent HTML/text content and message-level history are retained for 30 days; aggregate statistics are retained indefinitely; raw bounce details are kept for 7 days

facts.label: Account deletion and backup purge
facts.value: Exact time to purge all Transactional data and backups after account closure was not published in the Transactional terms, DPA or retention documentation checked

facts.label: Login security
facts.value: Mailchimp supports two-factor authentication by SMS or authenticator app; an Owner/Admin can require it for additional users

facts.label: Transactional roles and keys
facts.value: Transactional app access is limited to Mailchimp Owners/Admins; no separate roles within Transactional. API keys can be limited by IP and permitted methods; multiple keys/subaccounts support project separation.

facts.label: Name, official site and status
facts.value: Mailchimp Transactional; active hosted product; formerly called Mandrill

facts.label: Rebrand and status notices
