facts.label: Email API/SMTP billing unit
facts.value: Monthly quota counts sent and received emails together.

facts.label: Email Marketing billing units
facts.value: Email Marketing limits both stored contact addresses and monthly sends. Unsubscribed contacts remain stored and count toward the contact limit.

facts.label: Duplicate contacts across lists
facts.value: The pages reviewed do not say whether one address in multiple lists is counted once or more than once toward the account contact limit.

facts.label: Email API/SMTP free plan
facts.value: $0/month; 4,000 combined sent and received emails per month, 150/day, one sending domain, one user, and three-day email log retention.

facts.label: Older Email API/SMTP free quota
facts.value: An older sending-limits help article still says 3,500 free emails/month, while the current pricing page and a recent official price article say 4,000. Use 4,000 from the newer pricing page.

facts.label: Email Sandbox free plan
facts.value: $0/month; 50 test emails/month, one user, one sandbox, up to 10 stored messages in that sandbox, and no sandbox email address.

facts.label: Older Sandbox free quota
facts.value: The Sandbox troubleshooting page says 500 free emails/month, but current pricing lists 50. Use 50 from the newer pricing page.

facts.label: Email Marketing free plan
facts.value: $0/month; up to 500 contacts, 1,500 emails/month, one domain, one user, and no dedicated IP.

facts.label: Timed trial
facts.value: The pricing and billing pages show ongoing free plans. I found no timed trial duration or trial-only sending quota.

facts.label: Email API/SMTP paid entry
facts.value: Basic: $15/month for 10,000 emails/month; 3 users, 5 domains, and 5-day email logs. The pricing page shows monthly pricing.

facts.label: Email Sandbox paid entry
facts.value: Basic: $17/month, or $14/month equivalent with $168 billed annually; 500 tests/month, 3 users, one sandbox, 50 stored messages, and 100 forwarded emails/month.

facts.label: Email Marketing paid entry
facts.value: Essential: $15/month, or $12/month equivalent with $144 billed annually; 10,000 contacts and 30,000 sends/month.

facts.label: Annual billing and payment
facts.value: Annual subscriptions are available; billing FAQ says annual pricing is 20% lower. Monthly subscriptions require a credit card; annual payment can use card or bank transfer by request.

facts.label: Annual-price arithmetic
facts.value: Email Marketing Pro lists $47/month equivalent and $566 billed annually; 12 × $47 = $564, so those two displayed figures do not multiply exactly. Use the stated billed total rather than deriving an annual amount.

facts.label: Email API/SMTP overage
facts.value: The live price page lists overage rates per extra 1,000 messages: Basic $1; Business $0.88; Enterprise $0.55. Overages are capped; above the plan's cap, messages are rejected.

facts.label: Email Marketing overage and rollover
facts.value: Marketing FAQ says unused monthly email quotas do not roll over and additional sends are counted as overage. The current price page and reviewed FAQ do not publish the Marketing overage rate or numeric cap.

facts.label: Email Sandbox over-limit behavior
facts.value: Sandbox test quotas reset monthly, but the current price page and checked help pages do not establish a separate paid overage rate or exact over-limit action.

facts.label: Hosted service and sending costs
facts.value: Hosted products need no customer-operated server. API/SMTP and Marketing include sending in their separate plan quotas; Sandbox is for testing only.

facts.label: Taxes
facts.value: Subscription fees exclude applicable taxes, duties, and similar charges; the customer pays taxes other than Mailtrap's net-income taxes.

facts.label: Dedicated IP costs
facts.value: API/SMTP Business and higher plans include a dedicated IP; Email Marketing Pro includes one. No separate standalone IP add-on price was found.

facts.label: Mailtrap Local operating cost
facts.value: Mailtrap Local has an MIT license and no software price in its repository, but the user supplies a computer or server and manages its storage, updates, and backups. Exact operating cost depends on that setup.

facts.label: Reader fees and payouts
facts.value: No subscriber payment processor, revenue share, reader billing, or creator payout rules are published for Mailtrap Email Marketing.

facts.label: Monthly and daily sending caps
facts.value: Current API/SMTP price page lists 4,000 combined emails/month and 150/day on Free; paid plans show unlimited daily volume within monthly caps.

facts.label: API/SMTP hourly and connection limits
facts.value: Sending-limits guide says new accounts start at 150 emails/hour; paid accounts start around 600 or 800/hour, with soft-limit increases/support review. It also lists 10 concurrent SMTP connections per account and per IP, and 100 messages per connection.

facts.label: Message size and API batches
facts.value: API/SMTP email size is 10 MB by default; Business and higher can request up to 30 MB. API batch limit is 500 messages and 50 MB total payload.

facts.label: Marketing throttling
facts.value: Email Marketing can throttle UI campaigns up to 150,000 emails/hour, divided into 5-minute batches. This is user-controlled campaign pacing, separate from API/SMTP hourly limits.

facts.label: API request rate
facts.value: General API limit is 150 requests per 10 seconds per API token. Some endpoints have additional account-level limits.

facts.label: Customer countries
facts.value: Terms restrict use where export controls, sanctions, or local law prohibit it. The AUP names Russia, Belarus, embargoed countries, and listed restricted persons or entities.

facts.label: Customer-country eligibility
facts.value: Mailtrap does not publish a complete country-by-country signup or payment eligibility table in the checked Terms, AUP, and billing FAQ.

facts.label: Interface and support languages
facts.value: The marketing site has language options, but the checked pages do not establish which languages are supported in the product interface or customer support.

facts.label: Signup and age
facts.value: Terms require a registered account, business/professional/public-institution use, an authorized representative, and an adult user aged 18 or older. Free accounts are limited to one end user for one entity; commercial or multi-user use requires a paid plan with team members.

facts.label: Sending-domain approval
facts.value: Production sending requires a verified domain and compliance review. Automatic review usually takes a few minutes after DNS verification; additional or manual checks may take longer.

facts.label: Demo-domain restriction
facts.value: The supplied demo domain can send only to the email address used to register the account; users cannot create additional demo domains.

facts.label: Email Marketing setup
facts.value: Email Marketing campaigns cannot be sent until a sending domain has been added and verified.

facts.label: Email jobs
facts.value: Email API/SMTP handles transactional sending and bulk email through API or SMTP; Email Marketing handles newsletters and promotional campaigns through its web interface; Email Sandbox captures test mail; inbound email can be routed to an application.

facts.label: Hosting and sender dependency
facts.value: Email API/SMTP, Email Marketing, and Email Sandbox are hosted services. Production delivery is included in Email API/SMTP or Email Marketing; Sandbox captures messages without sending them to real recipients.

facts.label: Local install and external sender
facts.value: Mailtrap Local runs on the user's computer as a local catcher. Its default role is testing; a real delivery check can relay through a separately configured Mailtrap or external SMTP service.

facts.label: Paid newsletter subscriptions
facts.value: Mailtrap Marketing documents list management, campaigns, and automation, but does not publish reader checkout, recurring paid-subscription tiers, or access controls. Paid-reader monetization is not a documented product feature.

facts.label: Consent on import
facts.value: Email Marketing requires users to confirm they have permission to email imported contacts. Terms require specific consent and an up-to-date consent record for commercial mail.

facts.label: Unsubscribe and suppression
facts.value: Marketing emails include an unsubscribe option; unsubscribes are processed immediately and the contact is suppressed. The contact cannot be manually resubscribed and must opt in again.

facts.label: Signup and opt-out collection
facts.value: Marketing overview describes signup forms and requires a verified sending domain, but the pages checked do not establish form types, embedded form limits, or configurable double opt-in behavior.

facts.label: Marketing footer
facts.value: A physical mailing address, organization name, and contact email are required; Mailtrap says it can add a compliance footer when these are missing.

facts.label: Sending domains
facts.value: API/SMTP allows 1 domain on Free, 5 on Basic, 100 on Business, and unlimited on Enterprise. Marketing allows 1 on Free, 3 on Essential, and 100 on Pro.

facts.label: Domain authentication and tracking domain
facts.value: Users can verify a sending domain and configure a custom tracking subdomain. API/SMTP setup uses verification and DKIM CNAMEs, a tracking CNAME, and a DMARC TXT record.

facts.label: Brand and link domains
facts.value: Email Marketing pricing lists HTTPS link branding through the user's subdomain as a plan feature; the live comparison does not clearly state whether all Mailtrap branding can be removed from every email element.

facts.label: Writing and template tools
facts.value: Email Marketing offers a drag-and-drop editor, HTML/CSS code editor, reusable templates, and personalization with contact fields.

facts.label: Markdown editor
facts.value: No native Markdown writing editor was identified in the Email Marketing or API/SMTP documentation reviewed.

facts.label: Audience targeting
facts.value: Email Marketing supports static lists, dynamic segments, custom fields, and filters such as subscription status, list membership, and contact properties.

facts.label: Contact and user caps
facts.value: Email Marketing's live price page lists 500/10,000/25,000 contacts for the displayed Free/Essential/Pro tiers and 1/3/100 users.

facts.label: Company-level audience objects
facts.value: Team seats and subaccounts exist on higher plans, but the docs do not describe CRM-style company records as an audience object.

facts.label: Marketing automations
facts.value: Automations support contact-created, contact-field-updated, list-added/removed, and custom API-event triggers; actions include sending email, delays, conditional splits, and field/list changes.

facts.label: Automation limits
facts.value: Each contact may enter the same automation only once in 24 hours. Run-count limits vary by plan, but the exact numbers are shown only in the user's billing dashboard.

facts.label: External lifecycle events
facts.value: Custom API events can trigger automations. The reviewed docs do not establish native payment-provider triggers or detailed subscription-renewal/failure events.

facts.label: API and SMTP
facts.value: Email API/SMTP supports sending through REST API or SMTP; separate transactional and bulk-stream routes are documented.

facts.label: Official SDKs
facts.value: Official Mailtrap SDKs are documented for Node.js, Python, PHP, Ruby, Java, .NET, and Go.

facts.label: Integrations
facts.value: Official integration guides cover Make.com, Zapier, and n8n for adding/syncing contacts and events.

facts.label: Send events and inbound email
facts.value: Webhooks cover delivery, bounce, soft bounce, spam complaint, unsubscribe, open, click, suspension, and rejection. Inbound Email API receives messages and can fire webhooks.

facts.label: Webhook retry rules
facts.value: A webhook batch gets up to 40 retries at five-minute intervals, with a 30-second timeout. If it remains unsuccessful, Mailtrap pauses the webhook and notifies the user.

facts.label: Batch-send debugging
facts.value: Transactional API batch calls allow up to 500 messages and 50 MB total payload; a 200 response can contain individual message failures that must be checked.

facts.label: Send retries and idempotency
facts.value: The reviewed sending docs do not state an automatic retry guarantee for failed API sends or a duplicate-protection/idempotency window.

facts.label: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC
facts.value: Domain setup documents SPF, DKIM, DMARC, domain verification, and tracking records; the account generates required CNAME/TXT records.

facts.label: Bounce and complaint handling
facts.value: Email API/SMTP reports bounce, soft-bounce, spam-complaint, suspension, and rejection events; the current pricing page includes suppression management and bounce categorization.

facts.label: Marketing suppression
facts.value: Unsubscribed contacts are suppressed and cannot receive future campaigns. Bounced contacts have a bounced status and should not be re-added to a send.

facts.label: Thresholds and recovery
facts.value: No public complaint-rate shutdown threshold or complete suppression retention/export policy was found in the reviewed pages. API/SMTP pricing says suppressed addresses may be reverted.

facts.label: Sending-stream separation
facts.value: API/SMTP provides distinct transactional and bulk streams and endpoints. Email Marketing is a separately priced product with its own contacts and send quota.

facts.label: Shared and dedicated IPs
facts.value: API/SMTP Free and Basic do not include a dedicated IP; Business and Enterprise include one with automatic warm-up. Marketing Pro includes a dedicated IP.

facts.label: Cross-product IP isolation
facts.value: The reviewed pages do not say whether Marketing Pro's dedicated IP is isolated from API/SMTP sending or whether separate streams share account-level IP reputation.

facts.label: Reporting and tracking
facts.value: Email Marketing reports attempted, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced, spam complaints, and unsubscribes; recipient reports can be exported to CSV. API/SMTP exposes status and event history.

facts.label: Tracking controls
facts.value: API/SMTP open tracking can be turned off; click tracking is optional and requires a paid account. Marketing open-rate reporting uses a pixel and may be affected by image blocking and privacy tools.

facts.label: Automated activity filtering
facts.value: The reviewed analytics docs do not establish a complete bot-open or bot-click filtering feature for Marketing campaigns.

facts.label: Own-server setup and work
facts.value: Mailtrap Local is a single binary with embedded web UI and SQLite storage; it listens on localhost SMTP port 3535 and web/API port 3550. Users install/run it and maintain the computer, data, backups, and updates.

facts.label: Newsletter growth and revenue features
facts.value: Marketing docs show campaigns, signup forms, lists, segments, and automation; no reader referral, paid recommendation marketplace, ad placement, or sponsorship-sale tool is documented.

facts.label: Contact export
facts.value: Email Marketing exports selected contacts as CSV. The help FAQ says CSV includes custom fields and engagement data; the current contact guide says exports include contact fields and list memberships.

facts.label: Campaign-report export
facts.value: Email Marketing lets users download recipient reports in CSV format.

facts.label: List ownership and complete export
facts.value: The Terms and DPA establish customer-directed processing but I did not find an explicit statement that subscribers own the list or that every consent event, suppression history, and campaign asset is in one full export.

facts.label: Paid-subscriber migration
facts.value: Recurring paid-reader subscriptions and payment mandates are not a documented Mailtrap feature, so there is no Mailtrap payment migration path to assess.

facts.label: Data processors and locations
facts.value: The subprocessor list effective 2026-10-06 lists AWS and Google infrastructure in the United States and lists other data processors in the United States. The DPA provides transfer terms including the Data Privacy Framework and SCCs.

facts.label: Storage-region choice
facts.value: GDPR help says data is hosted in AWS us-east-1 and Google servers in the US and says EU-based storage was planned for 2026. The current subprocessor list still lists US locations; no current EU-only storage choice or launch notice was found.

facts.label: International transfers and agreements
facts.value: Privacy policy allows transfer/access from the US, EU, and other countries and describes safeguards; a DPA is published.

facts.label: Plan-based log and message retention
facts.value: API/SMTP log retention is 3/5/15/30 days and message-body retention is 3/5/7/15 days across Free/Basic/Business/Enterprise. Marketing shows 3/5/30-day logs and 3/5/15-day bodies for the displayed Free/Essential/Pro plans.

facts.label: Sandbox message retention
facts.value: Sandbox uses FIFO cleanup when an inbox's stored-message cap is reached; the user can clear the inbox. Privacy policy says test email content is deleted when the user clears the inbox or deletes the account.

facts.label: Account deletion
facts.value: On deletion request, account profile identifiers are deleted or redacted; usage/behavior data can remain pseudonymized for up to 90 days; sending content and logs are deleted within 30 days; server/application logs are kept no more than 30 days. Billing records may remain as required by law.

facts.label: Active contact retention
facts.value: The policy does not give a separate fixed expiration period for Marketing contact records while an account remains active; users can delete selected contacts in the contact manager.

facts.label: Two-factor authentication
facts.value: Current pricing tables list 2FA as an account safeguard.

facts.label: Roles and team access
facts.value: Account Owner/Admin/Viewer and domain/template roles are documented. Team-seat counts vary by product and plan; Enterprise offers SSO and subaccounts.

facts.label: API key permissions
facts.value: Email API/SMTP supports API-key permissions and shows which key sent a message in the email logs.

facts.label: IP allowlisting
facts.value: IP whitelisting is listed as a security feature for higher API/SMTP plans, not the Free or Basic tiers.

facts.label: Name and status
facts.value: Mailtrap is the current name for its three hosted products: Email API/SMTP, Email Sandbox, and Email Marketing. All are currently offered.

facts.label: Product change/history
facts.value: Mailtrap began as a testing tool; the company says Email API/SMTP and marketing email joined the platform in 2022.

facts.label: Shutdown, sunset, or acquisition notice
facts.value: No notice found in the checked About page, blog, or changelog. A separate newsroom page could not be checked.

facts.label: Human support
facts.value: Pricing lists email support on lower tiers and email plus live chat on premium tiers; standard support is Mon–Fri, while paid premium tiers show 24/7 availability.

facts.label: Public status page
facts.value: Mailtrap has a public status page. It showed all services online and 100% uptime, last updated 2026-11-05 13:32 UTC.

facts.label: Uptime statement
facts.value: About page claims a 99.99% uptime SLA, but the current Terms do not link an SLA or specify service credits in the reviewed sections.

facts.label: Source license and maintenance
facts.value: Mailtrap Local is in the official Mailtrap GitHub organization under MIT license. Latest release shown is v0.4.1, released 2026-09-07.

facts.label: Public history and scale
facts.value: Mailtrap says it began as an internal tool in 2011, became public in 2012, and grew beyond Sandbox in 2022. Its current About page claims 150K+ active customers, 2M+ signups, and 35+ people.

facts.label: Legal operator and country
facts.value: Railsware Products Studio LLC, incorporated in Delaware, United States, operates Mailtrap under the name Mailtrap. Its listed business address is in Pasadena, California.

facts.label: Billing unit

facts.label: Billing unit
facts.value: A request rejected at validation is not charged; delivered status means accepted by the recipient provider’s server, not inbox placement.

facts.label: Billing unit
facts.value: Rules for billing duplicate addresses or repeated entries across separate sends are not specified in the pricing page or billing FAQ.

facts.value: Each Tencent Cloud account receives a 1,000-email gift quota; usage beyond it is billed.

facts.label: Free plan and trial
facts.value: The docs do not say the 1,000-email gift quota renews monthly; recurring free allowance is not published.

facts.label: Free plan and trial
facts.value: No timed free trial, permanent no-cost sending plan, contact cap, or separate trial feature set was found in the official SES pricing/docs pages.

facts.label: Free plan and trial
facts.value: New sender domains start at 500 emails per day; daily limits can rise with domain reputation.

facts.label: Paid entry price
facts.value: Prepaid package rates are listed in USD on the international Indonesian-localized page; the page does not state which SES service region or account countries can buy them.

facts.label: Overage, caps, and rollover
facts.value: The newer page lists 600,000 emails for USD 144, 1,000,000 for USD 230, and 5,000,000 for USD 1,100; each package is valid six months.

facts.label: Overage, caps, and rollover
facts.value: SES bills pay-as-you-go usage daily from account balance; insufficient balance suspends service until funds are added.

facts.label: Overage, caps, and rollover
facts.value: Hitting the sender-domain daily reputation limit pauses and queues batch jobs for 24 hours; ordinary sends fail once the limit is reached.

facts.label: Total-cost extras
facts.value: Dedicated/independent IP is an optional add-on at USD 120 per IP per month; the pricing page gives no SES region or local-currency price split.

facts.label: Total-cost extras
facts.value: Dedicated IP inventory preparation may take 2–4 weeks; the service requires SES activation and a verified sending domain.

facts.label: Total-cost extras
facts.value: A sender domain, DNS hosting, mailbox, or tax may add separate costs; SES pricing does not include or quantify these costs.

facts.label: Fees, processors, and payout access
facts.value: Native paid-reader processor fees and creator payouts do not apply to the documented SES product.

facts.label: Technical sending limits
facts.value: New verified sender domain begins at 500 emails/day. Reputation levels scale to 1,000,000/day at Level 20; higher volume requires a support ticket.

facts.label: Technical sending limits
facts.value: Accounts activated on/after 2026-05-07 can raise each domain by at most one reputation level per calendar day; older accounts are exempt from this new daily cap.

facts.label: Technical sending limits
facts.value: Monthly maximum is the domain’s daily sending limit multiplied by 30.

facts.label: Technical sending limits
facts.value: Maximum 10 verified domains/account and 10 sender addresses/domain; the specs also list a maximum of 10,000 recipient addresses in a CSV batch, 50 per batch API call, and 20 in a regular console send.

facts.label: Technical sending limits
facts.value: SMTP send API rate: 20 calls/second per Tencent Cloud account appId; the same sender may send no more than 10 emails/hour to the same recipient.

facts.label: Technical sending limits
facts.value: SES request-structure guide lists a 1 MB POST limit for HMAC-SHA1/SHA256, up to 10 MB for TC3-HMAC-SHA256, and 32 KB for GET requests.

facts.label: Technical sending limits
facts.value: API attachment content is limited to 4 MB before base64 expansion; total request packet must stay within the API’s stated request limit.

facts.label: Technical sending limits
facts.value: When a batch hits the per-domain daily limit, unsent recipients queue and resume after 24 hours; ordinary sends over quota fail.

facts.label: Technical sending limits
facts.value: Newly activated individually verified accounts cannot use SMTP from 2026-03-02; no general sandbox-only recipient restriction was found in the product docs.

facts.label: Customer countries and markets

facts.label: Entry and approval rules
facts.value: Identity verification may be required during account setup; the vendor permits both individual and enterprise account types.

facts.label: Entry and approval rules
facts.value: A verified domain and sender address are prerequisites; SES template submissions are reviewed, with a stated target of one business day.

facts.value: Scheduled and recurring batch sends are supported; a native lifecycle journey builder is not described.

facts.value: Console sending can automatically insert an unsubscribe link; address-level unsubscribe configuration and event handling are available by API.

facts.label: Audience targeting

facts.value: Visual branching, journey exit rules, payment-event integrations, and native workflow-run limits are not published in SES docs.

facts.value: Idempotency key/window and inbound mail/reply processing were not found in API, SMTP, or callback documentation.

facts.label: Open/click event behavior
facts.value: Email webhooks send only the first open and unique link clicks per recipient

facts.label: Soft-bounce retries
facts.value: CPaaS retries temporary soft bounces periodically and later returns a hard-bounce status if delivery keeps failing; an exact retry count and schedule are not published

facts.label: Webhook retry guarantees
facts.value: Webhook retry count, retry window, and duplicate-event protection are not stated in the webhook guide

facts.label: Duplicate send protection
facts.value: An idempotency key or duplicate-send suppression window is not described for email API requests

facts.label: Inbound replies
facts.value: CPaaS documents outbound SMTP/API sends and delivery events; inbound mailbox or reply-processing APIs are not listed

facts.label: Domain authentication
facts.value: DKIM and a CNAME return-path record are required for domain verification; the domain guide says a separate SPF record is not required

facts.label: SPF requirement conflict
facts.value: The DMARC guide says CPaaS mandates SPF and DKIM verification, while the newer domain verification guide says DKIM and CNAME are needed and SPF is not required

facts.label: DMARC
facts.value: DMARC is documented as an additional domain policy that uses SPF and DKIM alignment to help receivers handle unauthenticated messages

facts.label: Bounce handling
facts.value: CPaaS records soft and hard bounces, retries temporary failures, and exposes bounce details in logs, reports, and webhooks

facts.label: Automatic suppression
facts.value: Auto-suppression is available for hard bounces such as domain, mailbox, or user not found; the scope can be one Agent or all Agents

facts.label: Manual recipient/domain suppression
facts.value: Users can manually block addresses or whole domains from email sending, and can separately block open/click tracking

facts.label: Complaint and bounce thresholds
facts.value: Terms set a bounce-rate threshold below 5%, spam complaints below 0.1%, and spam-trap/unjustified complaints below 1 per 100,000; Zoho may terminate accounts that exceed thresholds

facts.label: Shared IP
facts.value: Shared sending IP is the default for CPaaS email; Zoho can move sending back to shared IP if deliverability issues arise

facts.label: Dedicated IP eligibility
facts.value: Dedicated IP request is aimed at steady senders of at least 10,000 emails/day with bounce below 5% and spam complaints below 0.1%

facts.label: Dedicated IP availability
facts.value: Pricing currently names US, EU, and IN data centers; the help page says rollout is phased and to contact support for region availability

facts.label: Separate transactional and campaign streams
facts.value: CPaaS email infrastructure is described as isolated from marketing traffic; Agents split transactional sending by purpose or application

facts.label: Delivery and engagement reports
facts.value: Reports cover sent, delivered, soft/hard bounce, opens, clicks, and performance comparisons between Agents

facts.label: Tracking controls
facts.value: Open and click tracking can be enabled per Agent or overridden per message; a custom tracking CNAME is supported

facts.label: Bot and privacy filtering
facts.value: A documented automated-open or privacy-proxy filtering method is not published in the tracking and reports guides checked

facts.label: Revenue and campaign analytics
facts.value: Newsletter revenue attribution, campaign conversion reporting, and subscriber growth analytics are not applicable to this transactional sender

facts.label: Own-server setup and work
facts.value: Not applicable: customers integrate with Zoho's hosted SMTP/API service and do not install CPaaS on their own server

facts.label: Growth and newsletter income tools
facts.value: Not applicable: CPaaS has no creator referrals, sponsorship marketplace, ad sales, or paid-reader tools in its transactional email scope

facts.label: Separate Zoho Campaigns product
facts.value: Zoho points promotional and bulk email needs to Zoho Campaigns, a separate product with its own plan and customer-contact model

facts.label: List ownership and export
facts.value: CPaaS is not a newsletter contact-list manager; it sends to recipients supplied by an application or user request

facts.label: Email log export
facts.value: Email logs can be exported for the last 60 days as a ZIP; the export can include or exclude stored email content and filter by Agent

facts.label: Suppression export
facts.value: Suppression-list data can be exported, with a selected date range and suppression type

facts.label: Template export and complete data package
facts.value: A complete one-click export of all templates, recipient data, consent records, and all account data is not described in the export guide

facts.label: Paid-subscriber migration
facts.value: Not applicable: CPaaS does not manage paid newsletter subscriptions or reader payment relationships

facts.label: Account-region storage
facts.value: Current API docs list ten CPaaS data centers and map each account domain to a region; data is stored in the selected Zoho region

facts.label: Regional-list conflict
facts.value: Current CPaaS API documentation lists ten data centers; the CPaaS GDPR page lists six (US, EU, CN, IN, AU, JP)

facts.label: Encryption and transport
facts.value: CPaaS says email data is encrypted at rest and in transit; SMTP uses TLS and HTTPS protects web/API access

facts.label: Processing and DPA
facts.value: Zoho publishes a privacy policy and offers a Data Processing Addendum; DPA signing requires an organization administrator to request and sign it

facts.label: Backups and subprocessor locations
facts.value: Exact backup retention and CPaaS subprocessor locations for each of the ten account regions are not specified on the CPaaS GDPR page

facts.label: Email log and content retention
facts.value: Email log details are kept for 60 days; message content is stored for up to 60 days only when content retention is enabled

facts.label: Activity log retention
facts.value: CPaaS GDPR page states account activity logs are retained for one year

facts.label: Export archive duration
facts.value: Export help says a ZIP remains available three days in its summary but says two days in its detailed steps

facts.label: Deletion
facts.value: A Postmaster can initiate CPaaS account deletion; sending stops immediately, deletion can be reversed for 48 hours, and account data is removed after the closure process

facts.label: Multi-factor login
facts.value: Zoho Accounts supports optional MFA modes including OneAuth, authenticator codes, and security keys; an organization administrator can require MFA

facts.label: Roles and team access
facts.value: CPaaS roles are Postmaster, Engineer, and Viewer; access for Engineers and Viewers can be limited to selected Agents; up to 30 users

facts.label: API key and IP safeguards
facts.value: API keys are Agent-specific; sending can be restricted to approved IP addresses; keys can be generated or revoked by authorized users

facts.label: Separation between streams
facts.value: Agents separate domains, credentials, templates, logs, and controls for different sending purposes

facts.label: Name, official site, and status
facts.value: Zoho CPaaS; https://www.zoho.com/cpaas/; active hosted service

facts.label: Former product name
facts.value: ZeptoMail was renamed Zoho CPaaS on 2026-09-23

facts.label: Older name and continuity
facts.value: TransMail became ZeptoMail in 2021; the 2026 CPaaS rebrand preserves existing email integrations

facts.label: Support channels
facts.value: CPaaS publishes technical support by email and lists around-the-clock phone support; product material also lists chat

facts.label: Status page
facts.value: A public Zoho status service exists, but a CPaaS-specific status component could not be verified from its public page

facts.label: Service guarantee
facts.value: CPaaS terms do not guarantee delivery at all times and allow delays or non-delivery beyond Zoho's reasonable control

facts.label: Uptime SLA
facts.value: A public email-service uptime percentage or CPaaS-specific uptime SLA was not found in the product, contact, or terms pages checked

facts.label: Source license and maintenance
facts.value: Not applicable: Zoho CPaaS is a hosted service, not customer-installed software with a source license

facts.label: Public scale and history
facts.value: Zoho reported in Dec. 2022 that ZeptoMail had 37,000 organizations, 25,000 domains, and processed an average 250 million emails per month

facts.label: Owner and operator
facts.value: Zoho CPaaS is a Zoho product; CPaaS terms say the applicable Zoho entity provides the service based on customer region

facts.label: Headquarters / home region
facts.value: The product's applicable contracting entity varies by customer region; CPaaS product pages do not state one exclusive operating headquarters for this service

facts.label: Acquisition and product evolution
facts.value: Zoho introduced TransMail in 2020, renamed it ZeptoMail in 2021, and rebranded it Zoho CPaaS in 2026; no external acquisition is mentioned in the checked history

changes.label: Closing
changes.text: Hosted cloud closed 2026-10-31; self-hosted core remains
